QQmlTreeRow: Don't count the rows of a subtree recursively

QQmlTreeRow::subTreeSize(), used by QQmlTreeModel::treeSize(), called
subTreeSize() on each child, recursing once per level of the tree. A
tree nested deeply enough therefore exhausted the native stack when its
size was computed.

Count the rows iteratively instead, keeping the rows still to be
counted on an explicit stack.

QmlPreview: Load QML translations from qrc context URLs

ProxyTranslator::setLanguage() built the translation directory with
QUrl::toLocalFile(), which returns an empty string for qrc: URLs. When
the context URL pointed into resources, the .qm files were searched in
"/i18n" and never loaded, so no QML translation was applied.

This broke tst_qqmldebugtranslationservice on HarmonyOS, where test
data is built into resources and the data directory URL is
"qrc:/data/": all strings were reported as missing translations and no
elide warnings were produced.

Use QQmlFile::urlToLocalFileOrQrc() so that both local file and qrc
context URLs resolve to a path QTranslator::load() can handle.

Fix teardown hang with QuickPixmapReader

QQuickPixmapReader is a QThread subclass that encapsulates the thread
usage in the constructor/destructor.

The current code is broken if the QQmlEngine (and thus
QuickPixmapReader) are deleted as children of the QCoreApplication. At
this point no new events are posted and the deleteLater doesn't reach
the relevant thread. We then hang forever waiting on a thread that will
never quit.

The eventloop_hack was added in 2010
(ff983ee8257b79143911ca58ebedc49b1660a0c4 before Qt split) with the
comment that QThread::quit was not thread safe. Current docs say it is.

Dialogs: allow dialogs to open when the parent is a QWindow

Non-native dialogs require a parent window in order to open.
Normally this will be automatically detected by
QQuickAbstractDialog::windowForOpen(), which makes the assumption that
the parent of any dialog object is a QQuickItem.

In cases where a dialog object is created dynamically, and explicitly
given a QQuickWindow as the parent, this assumption would fail, and the
function would return nullptr, causing the dialog to not work.

The fix is simple, just check if the immediate parent object is a window
type, in which case, we use that as the dialogs parent. Otherwise, fall
back to the existing behavior of picking the parent item's render window.

QtQml: Look for AOT lookup signature imports in dependencies

A document can do lookups on a type it doesn't name, and whose module it
may not even import. It may get hold of the type via a property of a
type defined in a different document. The compiler then records the
import that other document has. The validator only looked at the imports
of the document itself, failed to find that import, and rejected a
valid compilation unit.

Also search the imports of the compilation units the compilation unit
depends on.

QtQml: Record import versions in AOT lookup signatures

A document can import the same module several times, with different
versions and qualifiers. Different versions of a module can provide
different types under the same name. The lookup signatures only
recorded the module and the type name, though. The validator resolved
the type through whichever import of the module it found first. If that
was an import of a different version than the one the compiler had seen,
we validated the lookup against the wrong type and rejected a valid
compilation unit.

Record the version of the import through which the type is found, and
only resolve the type through an import of exactly that module and
version. Also record the name the import provides the type under, rather
than the base name of the file. The two don't have to match.

This changes the layout of the lookup signatures. Bump the data
structure version.

QtQml: Resolve composite types for AOT validation via the CU's imports

The runtime validation of lookup signatures tried to find composite
types by guessing the module's location. It completed the module URI
against the import paths, picked the first qrc URL, re-parsed the qmldir
found there, and loaded the type from the file name listed in it. For
modules built with NO_RESOURCE_TARGET_PATH, the QML files and the qmldir
are not at qrc:/qt/qml/<module>/, though. Therefore, the validator could
not find the type, rejected the perfectly valid compilation unit, and
the engine silently fell back to the interpreter.

We don't have to guess. The compilation unit has already resolved all
its imports, and the module of any type it refers to must be among them.
Look up the import by module URI and resolve the type through it. Types
only referenced from script code are resolved, but not necessarily
loaded yet. Load them like QQmlTypeWrapper does.

QQmlTypeLoader::urlsForModule() is not needed anymore.

Skip tst_Snippets headerviewdelegate-custom on VxWorks

The qtquickcontrols-headerviewdelegate-custom snippet trips a QtQml bug:
a TableView/HeaderView delegate that declares or inherits a required
property evaluates its bindings with a null QQmlContextData while
QQmlObjectCreator::finalize() runs.
QQmlContextWrapper::getPropertyAndBase() then returns undefined (with
hasProperty set) for every unqualified name, so Math is undefined in the
style delegate's

implicitWidth: Math.max(implicitBackgroundWidth + ..., ...)

bindings. The implicit size stays zero and TableView warns that the
delegate's implicitWidth needs to be greater than zero, which fails the
test through QTest::failOnWarning().

This is not VxWorks specific. Everywhere else qmlcachegen AOT-compiles
those bindings into C++ that never consults the QML context, which hides
the problem; the VxWorks static cross build does not use the AOT
functions, so the JS path runs and the bug surfaces. It reproduces on
desktop Linux with QML_DISABLE_DISK_CACHE=1 or QV4_FORCE_INTERPRETER=1.

Skip the row on VxWorks until QTBUG-151176 is fixed, so the remaining
snippet rows keep guarding the VxWorks configuration.

StyleKitReader: emit style property changes on componentComplete

Style properties can be read from a StyleReader before it has been
completed, e.g. by the bindings of a control while it's being created.
At that point, the reader's own state (controlType, checked, hovered,
etc.) may not yet be fully initialized, so the values read can be
wrong. And since updateControl() is a no-op until m_completed is true,
and nothing was emitted from componentComplete(), state changes that
arrived after resetReadersForStyle() were never propagated. Bindings
could therefore be left with stale values based on the initial, and
wrong, state.

This patch fixes this by letting setCompleted() rebuild the effective
font and palette, and emit change signals for all style properties.
This forces any premature reads to be re-evaluated against the reader's
final state.

As a consequence, the reader is now added to s_allReaders on completion
rather than from the constructor, so that style and theme changes only
affect completed readers. For the same reason, onPaletteChanged() now
returns early until the reader is completed.

and verify that qml-jit is off.

QmlPreview: Parent rebuilt inner instances to their outer's new context

Rebuilding a component root replaces the contexts it is the context
object of: its outer context and the contexts of its composite base
levels. Instances of inner components created in one of those contexts
were then rebuilt with a new context parented to the old one. Ids of
the enclosing component resolved against the old context, whose
objects had been retired, and came back as null.

Record which contexts are replaced during a rebuild, and parent the new
contexts of later rebuilt instances to the replacements.

QmlPreview: Rebuild instances of inner components, don't remap by index

Instances of inner components (explicit or implicit Components) are not
always recreated when we rebuild the enclosing component. They survived
with their old binding values. Furthermore, after the rebuild we
remapped all objects still referring to the old compilation unit to the
new one, keeping their indices. If objects were added or removed in
front of them, those indices referred to unrelated objects. Rebuilding
such an object later, because its own composite type changed, applied
the unrelated object's bindings and property cache to it and crashed.

Treat the roots of inner components like any other component root.
Rebuild them in place if their index still denotes a component root in
the new compilation unit and their non-composite base type hasn't
changed. Otherwise rebuild the enclosing component, found by walking up
the QML context hierarchy, and fail if there is none. Contexts on the
way may have context objects that are not component roots at all, for
example the model items of delegates. Skip those.

Don't remap anything after a rebuild. Everything instantiated by the
old compilation unit has been recreated or rebuilt then. Whatever
survived without being rebuilt is obsolete. Retire it.

QQuickWindow: skip child window restacking when no child windows

QQuickWindowPrivate::dirtyItem() requests a child window stacking
order update whenever any item in the scene gets the
ChildrenStackingChanged dirty bit, which happens on every z change,
stackBefore/stackAfter, effective visibility change, and layer/effect
reference change. The next polishItems() then calls
updateChildWindowStackingOrder(), which walks the entire item tree,
calling paintOrderChildItems() and a qobject_cast on every item, to
raise embedded native child windows in paint order.

In typical scenes some item changes visibility or z nearly every
frame, so this full tree walk runs on almost every polish pass, even
in scenes without a single child window, where there is nothing to
restack.

The walk only raises windows whose parent window is this window, and
QWindow::setParent() also makes the window a QObject child of its
parent. So skip the deferred restacking in polishItems() when the
window has no direct QWindow child. The check is cheap, as it only
looks at the direct children of the window: the root item, the items
and value sources declared directly inside the Window in QML, and any
child windows. Other declared objects, including nested transient
Windows, are reparented to the content item. A window container
reparents its window in its own updatePolish(), which runs earlier in
the same polishItems(), so the restacking still happens in the pass
where the window arrives.

The synchronous restacking on ChildWindowAdded and SurfaceCreated is
unchanged, as is the behavior when child windows are present.

V4: Sign-extend heap pointers on 64-bit SPARC

Linux maps user memory above the VA hole on sparc64, from
0xfff8000100000000 on T4 and M7 and from 0xfff0000100000000 on M8 and
UltraSPARC III, so the heap pointers have their top bits set. The
sparc64 encoding kept bits 0-51 and required the rest to be clear, so
the engine crashed during start-up.

sign-extend from bit 56 when decoding. That covers the 44-, 48-, 52-
and 53-bit VA layouts the kernel uses on sparc64.

With GCC this branch is only compiled once qtbase defines
Q_PROCESSOR_SPARC_64 for it, see the qtbase commit
"qprocessordetection.h: Detect 64-bit SPARC when building with GCC".

In order to dismiss a Popup on a touch screen/mouse, we checked
if the we pressed outside the popup, and then we closed the popup.

deviceType() is TouchPad.

Qt::WA_AcceptTouchEvents under the popup, since we can synthesize
touchpad events ourselves from the autotest.

Drag.dragType: Drag.Automatic goes through QDrag::exec(), which blocks in a
nested event loop. Anything happening inside that loop can destroy the item the
Drag attached object belongs to -- a ListView recycling the delegate that is
being dragged is enough, which is what auto-scrolling during a drag does. Both
the QQuickDragAttached and the QDrag are QObject children of that item, so they
are deleted with it, and every line after exec() in startDrag() then runs on
freed memory: the reported crash is in the dragFinished() emission.

~QQuickItem notifies its change listeners before ~QObject deletes its children,
so that is the last point at which the drag can still be wound down by an object
that is still alive. Listen for Destroyed for the duration of a native drag and
do it from there: cancel the platform drag, which unwinds the nested loop and
delivers the drag leave that the drop target is waiting for, then report the
drag as finished and inactive. Guard the QDrag and the attached object itself
across exec() for whatever gets there first.

Nothing here knows about item views, so it covers TableView, PathView, Repeater
and plain delegate models as well, and any route to the item's destruction
rather than only recycling. It does not try to keep the item alive; an
application that wants the drag to survive can still use
ListView.delayRemove: Drag.active.

The new test drives the nested event loop, which needs a QPlatformDrag that runs
